title: Corn Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Learning

app.title: Corn Disease Detection & Advisory
app.description: A deployed Gradio app that detects corn leaf disease from an uploaded image and returns treatment advice.

shortSummary: A controlled comparison of DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B0 for corn leaf disease classification with transfer learning from ImageNet weights.
summary: A controlled comparison of two convolutional backbones, DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B0, for classifying corn leaf disease from images. The study was built around a question the accuracy headline usually hides: does an architecture comparison still hold once the split, the augmentation and the training budget are held fixed for both models?

variables.title: DenseNet121
variables.body: A densely connected backbone, where each layer receives the feature maps of every earlier layer. Included for its strong performance on small, fine-grained image datasets.

variables.title: EfficientNet-B0
variables.body: A compound-scaled backbone that balances depth, width and resolution. Included as the more parameter-efficient alternative to test whether fewer parameters cost anything in accuracy.

variables.title: Transfer learning from ImageNet
variables.body: Both models start from ImageNet weights rather than random initialisation, which is the realistic setting when labelled agricultural imagery is scarce.

statusNote: The dataset card, per-class metrics and the DenseNet121 / EfficientNet-B0 comparison table are published together with the thesis document, so the numbers here stay traceable to the report rather than being quoted from memory. The LaTeX source and figures live in the public repository.
limitations: Corn leaf disease is a narrow slice of agricultural vision: results here should not be read as evidence about field conditions, occlusion or other crops.
A two-model comparison is a starting point, not a survey — the honest conclusion is about these two backbones under one fixed protocol.
Reported accuracy is only meaningful alongside the split it was measured on, which is why the protocol is documented before the number.
